notes: Run only with approval. The prompts are in English, so every deliverable and gate question must be in English too. Each eval fails if the manual is skipped or a template is generated before an explicit ok, if a missing fact is invented instead of written as [placeholder], if check_page.py reports an ERROR, or if the delivered formats differ only in color and font instead of composition, type, shape and color. The brand-kit is the default proof of the system and is skipped only for a single-artifact request. The v2 contract is final: no v1 fields, no product flavor and no Gupy tokens.

evals.prompt: I am opening a small wood-fired pizzeria in a converted garage. I only have a loose terracotta color and a phone photo of the oven; the name might still change and I have no logo. I need a brand I can defend, a manual my partner will approve, and something I can put online this week.
evals.expected_output: Recommend 2-3 named routes with palette, type, shape and composition for each, and state the visual difference between them before generating anything; wait for the user's route choice. Then generate brand.json, theme.css, tailwind-theme.css and logo.svg. Generate manual.html and stop at Gate 2 for an explicit ok before any template. After approval, generate onepage.html (the landing sells the opening) and social.html (1080x1080 and 1080x1920 mockups, not PNG export). Use placehold.co for the oven and product photos while the real shoot does not exist, and Iconify for menu and contact icons. Keep the final name, address, prices and testimonials as [placeholder] and list them in the delivery note; never invent proof. The visual difference must show up in composition (poster-like hero, generous margins), type (a warm serif display against a humanist sans), shape (soft 4/8/12/16/24 radii) and color (terracotta canvas with a cream accent), not just a palette swap. Generate brand-kit.html by default as the proof of the system; skip it only if the user asks for a single artifact. check_page.py must report zero ERROR on manual, onepage and social, and the reply must say whether the browser pass ran. Reply in English.

evals.prompt: I need a brand for a small B2B consultancy that helps industrial clients with operations strategy. I have no logo, only a dark green I like and two reference screenshots. I need a manual, a landing page, a deck for sales meetings and a client report.
evals.expected_output: Recommend 2-3 named routes and wait for the route choice. Then generate brand.json, theme.css, tailwind-theme.css and logo.svg. Generate manual.html and stop at Gate 2 for an explicit ok before any template. After approval, generate onepage.html (the landing sells), deck.html (1280x720 slides that present) and report.html (explains, with tables that have a caption and scoped th). Each format gets its own copy, not the same paragraph reused. Use Iconify for interface icons, Chart.js only on report.html for the operating trend with a table fallback, and placehold.co for client logos and screenshots until real assets exist. Keep unknown client names, metrics, dates and case results as [placeholder] and list them in the delivery note; never invent proof. The visual difference must be visible in composition (editorial grid with a measured column), type (condensed display against a neutral grotesk), shape (8px unit with restrained 4/8/12 radii) and color (deep green with a chalk surface), not only in color and font. Generate brand-kit.html by default as the proof of the system; skip it only if the user asks for a single artifact. check_page.py must report zero ERROR on manual, onepage, deck and report, and the reply must say whether the browser pass ran. Reply in English.

evals.prompt: We are a small independent record label with a brutalist streak. I want a poster for our next release and matching social posts, plus the brand manual so the next designer does not soften it. Everything should feel raw, loud and printed, not corporate.
evals.expected_output: Recommend 2-3 named routes and wait for the route choice. Then generate brand.json, theme.css, tailwind-theme.css and logo.svg. Generate manual.html and stop at Gate 2 for an explicit ok before any template. After approval, generate blank.html as the A2 poster (the skeleton is a starting point; compose it from sections.md) and social.html as 1080x1080 and 1080x1920 mockups, not PNG export. No Chart.js on either file: this is a type-led identity, not a report. Use Iconify only if a meaningful symbol is needed, with a text label, and placehold.co only if a photo is unavoidable; prefer CSS texture over stock imagery. Keep dates, catalog numbers, track titles and quotes as [placeholder] and list them in the delivery note; never invent releases. The visual difference must come from composition (poster grid with hard alignment), type (black condensed display and monospace body), shape (sharp 0/0/2/4/4 radii, unit 4, no shadows) and color (signal orange against asphalt grey), not just a loud palette. Generate brand-kit.html by default as the proof of the system; skip it only if the user asks for a single artifact. check_page.py must report zero ERROR on manual, poster and social, and the reply must say whether the browser pass ran. Reply in English.

evals.prompt: We are launching a small-batch luxury perfume. The brief is silence, glass and old gold; the customer collects scent the way others collect watches. I need the brand book, a landing page and a presentation for select retailers. No discount language, no celebrity.
evals.expected_output: Recommend 2-3 named routes and wait for the route choice. Then generate brand.json, theme.css, tailwind-theme.css and logo.svg. Generate manual.html and stop at Gate 2 for an explicit ok before any template. After approval, generate onepage.html (the landing sells the object, not a promotion) and deck.html for the retailer presentation, each with its own copy. Do not load Chart.js: there is no data story here. Use placehold.co for the bottle and campaign photography until the real shoot exists, and Iconify sparingly for navigation only. Keep the launch date, price, stockists and perfumer names as [placeholder] and list them in the delivery note; never invent provenance. The visual difference must be carried by composition (minimal measured column and generous negative space), type (high-contrast serif display with a light sans), shape (barely-there 0/2/4 radii, unit 8, strong shadows kept soft) and color (near-black canvas with old gold and deep plum), not just a dark palette. Generate brand-kit.html by default as the proof of the system; skip it only if the user asks for a single artifact. check_page.py must report zero ERROR on manual, onepage and deck, and the reply must say whether the browser pass ran. Reply in English.

evals.prompt: A kids science museum needs a new brand for a family audience. It should feel curious and playful without becoming a cartoon, and it has to work for parents on a phone as well as for printed posters at the entrance. I need a landing page and social posts for the opening season.
evals.expected_output: Recommend 2-3 named routes and wait for the route choice. Then generate brand.json, theme.css, tailwind-theme.css and logo.svg. Generate manual.html and stop at Gate 2 for an explicit ok before any template. After approval, generate onepage.html (the landing sells the visit) and social.html (1080x1080 and 1080x1920 mockups, not exports). Use Iconify for the family of exhibit and wayfinding icons, and placehold.co for exhibit photography until the real images exist. Do not load Chart.js: this is not a data page. Keep opening dates, ticket prices, exhibit names and testimonials as [placeholder] and list them in the delivery note; never invent facts for children. The visual difference must come from composition (structured but playful blocks with a clear reading order), type (rounded display with a highly legible body), shape (round 8/12/16/24/9999 radii, unit 8) and color (bright primary blue with warm yellow and green accents), and the result must differ from a generic kids template in composition and type, not just in color. Generate brand-kit.html by default as the proof of the system; skip it only if the user asks for a single artifact. check_page.py must report zero ERROR on manual, onepage and social, and the reply must say whether the browser pass ran. Reply in English.

evals.prompt: I only need one thing: an internal operations dashboard for our team, using our existing brand. It should show the queue, the week trend and the exception list, with empty and error states. No landing page, no deck and no social posts.
evals.expected_output: Run discovery and the mandatory manual even for a single artifact: recommend 2-3 named routes and wait for the route choice, then generate brand.json, theme.css, tailwind-theme.css and logo.svg, generate manual.html and stop at Gate 2 for an explicit ok before any template. After approval, generate only app.html with a topbar, sidebar, page header, stats, queue table, filters, empty/loading/error states, a modal and a form, all with the same tokens and a denser rhythm. Use Chart.js for the week trend with an accessible table fallback, and Iconify for navigation and state icons. Do not clone a generic SaaS dashboard: the screen must carry this brand's composition (compact editorial grid), type (distinct display and body roles), shape (the brand's radius profile and shadow level) and color (the brand's roles), so the visual difference is not just a palette swap. No Chart.js anywhere else and no borrowed product UI. Skip brand-kit.html because the user asked for one artifact, and say so in the delivery note. Keep team names, metric values, dates and exception descriptions as [placeholder] and list them in the delivery note; never invent operational data. check_page.py must report zero ERROR on manual and app, and the reply must say whether the browser pass ran. Reply in English.
